papers.title: Molecular Cloning of Oxytocin and Oxytocin Receptor Genes and Their Ligand-Receptor Binding in the Root Vole (Microtus oeconomus).
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The root vole (Microtus oeconomus), a small mammal native to the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau, is adapted to chronic high-altitude hypoxia and exhibits a polygynous mating system. whereas the prairie vole (Microtus ochrogaster) from North American grasslands is a model of social monogamy. Oxytocin (OXT) and its receptor (OXTR) play central to prosocial behaviors including pair bonding, yet their sequences and evolutionary implications in the root vole remain unclear. METHODS: we retrieved cytochrome b, OXT, and OXTR sequences from 21 species via GenBank. Coding and regulatory regions of the OXT and OXTR in the root vole were cloned by PCR, nucleotide and amino acid sequences were aligned using DNAMAN 6 and Multalin tool. Phylogenetic trees were constructed in MEGA X using the neighbor-joining (NJ) method. The three-dimensional (3D) structures of the OXT-OXTR complexes for mouse, M. oeconomus, and M. ochrogaster were predicted with AlphaFold 3. and Hydrogen bonds were analyzed in ChimeraX (1.11.1). RESULTS: We cloned the OXT and OXTR coding and regulatory regions from hypothalamus of M. oeconomus. Phylogenetic trees placed M. oeconomus, M. ochrogaster, and Mus musculus in a single major clade, with the two-vole species sharing the same branch. Species-specific sequence variations between the two voles were identified. Predicted 3D structures revealed differences in ligand-receptor binding interfaces and in hydrogen-bond networks across species. Notably, the M. ochrogaster complex contained the greatest number of hydrogen bonds, suggesting a tighter ligand-receptor interaction. CONCLUSION: We propose that variation in the OXT-OXTR hydrogen-bond network, the ligand-binding pocket (TM4), and the intracellular loops IC1 and IC3 may be related to underlie species differences in ligand-receptor binding affinity and, consequently, in pair-bonding behavior.

papers.title: Early acting components of courtship contribute to prezygotic reproductive isolation between closely related Chorthippus grasshopper species.
RDX-Associated Hearing Loss: Expanded Variant Spectrum, Founder Effect, and Mechanistic Insights from Functional Assays.
papers.journal: Genetics in medicine : official journal of the American College of Medical Genetics
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Bi-allelic RDX variants are responsible for DFNB24, a type of autosomal recessive nonsyndromic hearing loss. Due to its rarity, the mutational spectrum, genotype-phenotype correlations, and population genetics of this condition are not yet fully understood. METHODS: We performed exome or targeted panel sequencing, along with segregation analysis, and evaluated clinical data. We conducted minigene assays on three intronic variants, with canonical splice-site variants included as positive controls, and used molecular dynamics simulations to explore the predicted conformational effects of missense and in-frame deletion alleles. Additionally, we compiled a systematic review of all previously reported DFNB24 families. RESULTS: We identified 12 distinct bi-allelic RDX variants in 16 families, six of which were novel. Those affected experienced bilateral, prelingual, or early childhood onset of sensorineural hearing loss, with varying degrees of severity. Minigene assays demonstrated variant-specific activation of cryptic splice sites for all three intronic variants, generating frameshift transcripts predicted to result in loss of function. Exome-derived haplotype and founder-dating analyses identified two distinct shared ancestral haplotypes among the Iranian families. Probands homozygous for c.1076_1079del, an allele found in four unrelated families, shared a 2.44-Mb haplotype with a most recent common ancestor approximately 386 years ago (95% CI, 83.7-677.7 years), whereas the two probands homozygous for c.1729A>T (Families 14 and 16) shared a 7.88-Mb haplotype dating to approximately 99.9 years ago (95% CI, 24.3-521.1 years), indicating a single ancestral event rather than two independent observations. The systematic review showed that reported DFNB24 families were concentrated in Middle Eastern and South Asian populations. papers.title: Navigating modern intimacy: a qualitative exploration of the influence of hook-up culture on experiences of sex and relationships.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Hook-up culture refers to a social environment where uncommitted sexual encounters are accepted and encouraged, often facilitated by dating apps such as Tinder. This culture normalises non-committed sexual interactions, where romantic exclusivity, emotional intimacy and monogamy are not considered prerequisites for having sex. There is limited research into how hook-up culture may influence future committed relationships and studies primarily draw upon college-aged student samples in the United States. OBJECTIVES: To address these gaps, the present study aimed to answer the research question: "How does participating in hook-up culture influence people's self-reported experiences of sex and relationships?". METHOD: Using an Australian sample, qualitative surveys were completed by 41 participants. Data were analysed thematically. RESULTS: Four overarching themes were developed: Adjusting to Commitment, Realising Self-Worth, Prioritising Connection and Intimacy and Conflicting Sexual Norms. Findings provide insights into the challenges of transitioning from hooking up to a committed relationship and how this can influence self-reported relationship dynamics, sexual health and individual psychosocial wellbeing. CONCLUSIONS: The ambiguity surrounding boundaries and definitions of casual sexual relationships was evident. Implications for psychological care are discussed. Further research is needed to explore the experiences of diverse populations within hook-up culture to gain a more comprehensive understanding of its dynamics and implications. papers.title: Construction of Electroneutral Meso-Amide-BODIPY-Based AIE Fluorescent Probes for Lipid-Droplet Viscosity Imaging.
papers.abstract: Fluorescent molecular rotors for cellular viscosity have been widely developed to investigate the close relationships of viscosity with many associated diseases, among which the lipid-droplet (LD)-targeting and aggregation-induced emission (AIE)-type ones remain rarely reported. To realize these LD-targeting and AIE characters, herein, we first designed four electroneutral meso-amide BODIPY-based molecular rotors, explored viscosity/AIE properties, and cellular imaging for LD viscosity. Interestingly, by introducing the meso-amide-rigid phenyl group, BDP-Ph exhibited enhanced fluorescence at 526 nm in high viscous glycerol and AIE in water, while further introducing CF3, BDP-CF3Ph showed improved viscosity sensing properties and AIE in 80% water. In contrast, with the meso-amide-flexible groups (benzyl and n-butyl), BDP-Bn and BDP-Bu displayed moderate viscosity response performance and better AIE character even in pure water, which can be attributed to the presence of flexible groups avoiding the formation of large aggregates. Then, BDP-Ph and BDP-CF3Ph were chosen to evaluate the bioimaging for viscosity in living cells, which exhibited no toxicity and successfully responded to elevated intracellular viscosity through pretreatment with lipopolysaccharide and monensin. According to the similar structure with BODIPY 493/503, LD targeting subcellular localization experiments revealed that BDP-Ph and BDP-CF3Ph showed good Pearson's correlation coefficients as high as 0.92 and 0.90, respectively. Fluorescence enhancements and numbers of LDs were clearly observed in oleic acid-induced lipid accumulation and autophagy models. Therefore, we for the first time reported and systematically investigate the meso-amide BODIPY-based electroneutral probes as AIE fluorescent rotors for cellular viscosity imaging in LDs.

papers.title: Genomic signatures of divergence and connectivity in the Western Banded Gecko (Coleonyx variegatus).
papers.abstract: Desert ecosystems of the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico are characterized by high endemism. Many desert adapted species exhibit phylogeographic patterns that correlate with major desert regions, but the relative contributions of geographic isolation, environmental differentiation, and gene flow to these patterns remain unclear. In this study, we used genome-wide SNP data to measure the genetic diversity of the Western Banded Gecko (Coleonyx variegatus), which spans the Sonoran and Mojave deserts, and the entirety of the Baja California Peninsula. The broad geographic distribution of C. variegatus across these unique ecosystems provides an opportunity to determine how genetic diversity is structured across desert ecoregions, and to investigate the history of gene flow within and between deserts. We conduct population structure analyses to identify population boundaries, use multispecies coalescent models to estimate the species tree and divergence times, and then apply the multispecies coalescent with migration (MSC-M) to estimate rates of gene flow among populations. Our analyses identify geographically and genetically distinct populations that largely align with desert ecoregions. Populations exhibit significant ecological niche differentiation; however, counter to expectations, high levels of gene flow persist, particularly between populations in the Mojave and Sonoran deserts. Species tree inference and divergence dating suggest a recent diversification history, with primary lineages originating during the mid-to-late Pleistocene. These results contribute to a growing phylogeographic framework for taxa spanning the southwestern deserts and highlight the value of comparative analyses across sympatric species for identifying shared drivers of diversification in the region.

papers.title: Quality of life, perceived stress, and coping strategies in Italian women with endometriosis: A cross-sectional online survey.
papers.journal: European journal of obstetrics, gynecology, and reproductive biology
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Endometriosis is a chronic gynaecological condition that may affect physical health, psychological well-being, fertility, intimate relationships, and social and occupational functioning. This study examined quality of life, perceived stress, and coping strategies in Italian women with self-reported physician-diagnosed endometriosis. METHODS: A cross-sectional online survey was conducted among 446 Italian women reporting physician-diagnosed endometriosis. Participants completed the Endometriosis Impact Questionnaire (EIQ), the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS-10), and the COPE-NVI-25. Analyses included one-way analysis of variance, Pearson correlations, and multivariable linear regression with heteroscedasticity-consistent standard errors; false-discovery-rate adjustment was applied to exploratory comparisons. RESULTS: Mean age was 32.5 ± 8.1 years, and mean reported age at diagnosis was 26.8 ± 6.3 years. EIQ scores were highest in the physical and psychological domains, particularly among women diagnosed within the previous year. Perceived stress increased consistently with the frequency of all disease-related difficulties examined. PSS-10 scores correlated positively with all EIQ domains, most strongly for the psychological (r = 0.551; 95 % CI 0.483 to 0.613), social (r = 0.511; 95 % CI 0.439 to 0.577), and physical (r = 0.451; 95 % CI 0.374 to 0.522) domains, negatively with positive attitude (r = -0.412; 95 % CI -0.486 to -0.332) and problem-focused coping (r = -0.291; 95 % CI -0.374 to -0.204), and positively with avoidance strategies (r = 0.335; 95 % CI 0.250 to 0.415; all p < 0.001). In multivariable analysis, higher PSS-10 scores were independently associated with greater EIQ total score, lower positive attitude, higher avoidance strategies, and poor/fair self-

papers.title: Feasibility and Preliminary Efficacy of a Novel Online Prevention Program Addressing Changes to First-Time Parent Couples' Sexual Well-Being.
papers.abstract: The perinatal period brings persistent changes to couples' sexual and romantic relationships. Access to perinatal sexuality information benefits sexual well-being, yet sexual health remains neglected in perinatal care. We examined feasibility and preliminary efficacy of the first couple-based online prevention program (Supporting the Transition to Parenthood through Online Sexual and Relationship Knowledge; STORK) targeting perinatal sexual challenges via psychoeducation and cognitive-behavioral skill-building. We examined feasibility (practicality, acceptability, demand) via adherence and self-reports, and preliminary efficacy by comparing primary (sexual satisfaction, desire, distress) and secondary (relationship satisfaction, relationship conflict, depressive symptoms) outcomes among expectant couples with STORK program access (N = 45 woman-man dyads) and a matched control sample from mid-pregnancy/pre-program to three months postpartum/post-program. Feasibility was strong. Most couples adhered to the STORK program and rated it highly. Preliminary efficacy findings were small-to-moderate and positive for birthing parents but mixed for partners. Compared to controls, birthing parents reported smaller declines in sexual satisfaction and desire and smaller increases in conflict and depressive symptoms. Relationship satisfaction declined less for both parents. Unexpectedly, partners reported greater declines in desire and increases in sexual distress. STORK addresses a critical gap in perinatal care by offering an accessible program to support couples' adjustment, especially for birthing parents.

papers.title: tRNA database 2026, extended compilation of tRNA sequences and tRNA genes.
papers.abstract: The tRNAdb database, published >15 years ago, originated as an extension of Mathias Sprinzl's seminal collection of transfer RNA (tRNA) data dating back to the late 1970s. Throughout its lifespan, the tRNAdb has been used extensively, accumulating >1000 citations. Here, we present tRNAdb 2026, https://tdb.bioinf.uni-leipzig.de/, an updated version hosted at Leipzig University. The tRNAdb 2026 features an ~10-fold increase in data coverage, containing >500 000 new mitochondrial and nuclear tRNA sequences together with the unaltered legacy dataset. Importantly, identifiers and metadata of the legacy dataset remain consistent with the original database, ensuring that previously published references remain valid and findable. The expanded dataset integrates publicly available tRNA annotations and sequences generated using contemporary prediction pipelines followed by semiautomated curation to ensure annotation quality and consistency. In addition, cross-references to external resources such as gtRNAdb facilitate interoperability with existing tRNA annotation frameworks. A modern web-based frontend provides intuitive and efficient access to tRNAdb 2026, while an Application Programming Interface enables automated data retrieval and integration into bioinformatics workflows. To support transparent scientific documentation and reproducibility across future updates, we added a versioning system for both current and future database releases.

papers.title: Effects of Aggregation-State Structure on Intrinsic Room-Temperature Phosphorescence in Semi-Aromatic Polyamides.
papers.abstract: Room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) in polymers is generally considered to benefit from restricted molecular motion and increased crystallinity. However, the relationship between aggregation-state structure and RTP performance in hydrogen-bond-rich polymers remains insufficiently understood. Herein, semi-aromatic polyamides with distinct aromatic structural configurations were employed as model systems to systematically investigate the influence of aggregation-state structure on intrinsic RTP. All polyamides exhibit long-lived RTP associated with cluster-triggered emission (CTE) states arising from interactions between amide groups and aromatic structural units. Notably, despite comparable proportions of hydrogen-bond-associated carbonyl groups, isophthalic acid-based polyamides exhibit longer phosphorescence lifetimes and more persistent afterglow than their terephthalic acid-based counterparts. Combined structural characterization and photophysical analyses reveal a close relationship between differences in aggregation-state structure and phosphorescence behavior. In particular, the less ordered isophthalic acid-based polyamides exhibit superior RTP performance, indicating that high crystallinity is not a prerequisite for efficient intrinsic phosphorescence in these systems. These performance differences may be associated with the interplay between local molecular confinement and triplet-exciton dynamics. This work establishes an important correlation between aggregation-state structure and intrinsic RTP performance in semi-aromatic polyamides, providing new insights into polymer structure-phosphorescence relationships and the design of intrinsic phosphorescent materials with persistent afterglow.

papers.title: Emergent parallels between language models and the brain.
papers.abstract: How does the brain give rise to human capabilities like language processing or logical reasoning? This question has captured the minds of many cognitive scientists and neuroscientists, and indeed has a history dating back at least as far as the philosophers of ancient Greece. Until recently, humans were the only systems that we knew of that showed these capacities across broad domains. But after recent developments in the field of artificial intelligence, language models have begun to show some surprising parallels to complex cognitive capacities and the neural representations that underpin them - despite the architectures and learning paradigms of these models differing dramatically from biological systems. In this primer, I will provide a brief overview of language models, their construction and training, and the phenomena of natural intelligence that they might help us to understand. First, let us begin with a bit of history.

papers.title: Centennial-scale effects of anthropogenic pollution and sedimentary processes on benthic foraminiferal assemblages in Gamak Bay, South Korea.
papers.abstract: Gamak Bay, South Korea, has experienced recurrent hypoxia amid urbanization and aquaculture. We integrated surface sediment distribution with geochemical and benthic foraminiferal records from three 210Pb-dated sediment cores spanning ca. 1904-2014. Mean CRS-derived sediment accumulation rates were 0.44, 0.60, and 1.19 cm yr-1 in cores 11257, 10863, and 11285, respectively. Despite similar grain-size compositions, the cores recorded contrasting sedimentary and geochemical histories. Sediment accumulation increased most markedly in the northwestern inner-bay core 11285 after ca. 1960, accompanied by greater organic enrichment and lower C/S ratios. Concentration factors and pollution load index values indicated modest increases in metal concentrations relative to core-specific historical reference levels, but these increases were not consistently greatest in core 11285. Core 11257 retained a diverse, stable assemblage, whereas core 10863 shifted toward greater Elphidium subarcticum dominance around the mid-1980s. Core 11285 showed persistently low diversity and pronounced assemblage changes, from Ammonia beccarii-rich assemblages before ca. 1961, through compositionally variable assemblages during ca. 1964-1975, to assemblages rich in E. subarcticum and agglutinated taxa after ca. 1977. These changes broadly coincided with urbanization and aquaculture development. Principal component analysis revealed core-specific geochemical-faunal associations, including positive PC1 loadings of organic enrichment-related variables and selected taxa in core 11285. These findings suggest that benthic deterioration in the northwestern inner bay was more closely associated with local depositional conditions and sustained organic enrichment than with overall trace metal accumulation. The results highlight the value of integrating sedimentological, geochemical, and foraminiferal records to distinguish spatially variable responses to anthropogenic pressures.

papers.title: Microbial succession and functional gene repertoires in Brassica rapa fermentation.
papers.abstract: Traditional fermented vegetables are complex microbial ecosystems whose dynamics are shaped by processing conditions, yet many regional European fermentations remain poorly characterized. This study combined shotgun metagenomics, culture-dependent analyses, and chemical measurements to characterize microbial succession, fermentation dynamics, and metagenomic functional potential during brovada fermentation and to compare one semi-industrial and one artisanal production system over 30 days. The two systems showed distinct trajectories. In the semi-industrial system, lactic acid bacteria (LAB) increased to 8.30 ± 0.50 log CFU/g by day 30, together with rapid sugar depletion, lactic acid accumulation, and a final pH of 3.94 ± 0.09. In the artisanal system, LAB peaked at 5.63 ± 0.38 log CFU/g at day 9 and declined to 3.92 ± 0.26 log CFU/g, while the final pH remained higher (4.51 ± 0.08); yeasts became more abundant than LAB at the end of fermentation. Metagenomic profiling showed a faster transition from Proteobacteria- to Firmicutes/LAB-dominated communities in the semi-industrial system, whereas the artisanal system retained greater microbial diversity and a longer persistence of Pseudomonas, Acinetobacter, and other environmental taxa. Functional profiling identified genes associated with bile salt hydrolysis, adhesion, exopolysaccharide production, gamma-aminobutyric acid (GABA) synthesis, plantaricin production, myrosinase-like activity, nitrate/nitrite metabolism, and amino acid and folate biosynthesis. Overall, the study shows that brovada fermentation can follow markedly different microbial and metabolic trajectories under contrasting production conditions, with corresponding differences in functional gene repertoires. These findings highlight the close relationship between processing conditions, microbial succession, and the functional potential of traditional vegeta

papers.title: Decoupling the Intrinsic Li/Mn Disorder Mechanism in Li-Rich Layered Oxides.
papers.abstract: Li-rich layered oxides (LLOs) are promising high-energy cathodes but suffer from irreversible oxygen redox and structural degradation associated with Li2MnO3 domains. Recently, disorder engineering has emerged as an effective strategy to regulate the local coordination environment and stabilize the oxygen redox of LLOs. Herein, we confirm the existence of intrinsic intralayer Li/Mn disorder within the Li2MnO3 domains, which can be classified into local Li-excess and TM-excess configurations derived from the initial Li-rich framework. Furthermore, DFT calculations suggest complementary local roles for the different disordered configurations: Li-excess domains promote oxygen redox activity, whereas TM-excess domains reinforce TM-O bonding and stabilize the framework against irreversible degradation. Consequently, M-LLO containing the coupled disordered configurations promotes more reversible anionic redox, suppresses irreversible oxygen release and transition-metal migration, and thereby delivers improved electrochemical stability. This work provides new insights into the role of intrinsic disorder regulation in Li-rich layered cathodes.

papers.title: Multimodal Imaging of Oxidized Low-Density Lipoprotein in Living Systems with Engineered Fluorescent Protein Chromophores.
papers.abstract: Targeted, high-fidelity visualization of oxidized low-density lipoprotein (Ox-LDL) in complex living biological systems remains a longstanding bioanalytical bottleneck for investigating metabolic liver and cardiovascular diseases. This limitation stems from the heterogeneous, poorly defined structure of the Ox-LDL and the lack of molecular probes with adequate target specificity. Herein, we describe a bioinspired molecular engineering strategy to generate a series of probes derived from green fluorescent protein (GFP) chromophores. To the best of our knowledge, the lead candidate 1j (MW = 387.2 Da) is the smallest synthetic probe reported for Ox-LDL targeting. Upon Ox-LDL binding, 1j exhibited a 98-fold fluorescence turn-on response. This effect arose from restricted twisted intramolecular charge transfer (TICT), coupled with specific hydrogen-bonding interactions with apolipoprotein B100 (ApoB100) embedded in Ox-LDL particles. The proposed mechanism was supported by density functional theory (DFT) calculations, molecular docking, and 1H NMR spectroscopy. Probe 1j selectively distinguished high-density lipoprotein (HDL), low-density lipoprotein (LDL), and Ox-LDL in live-cell assays. Quantitative fluorescence-lifetime imaging microscopy (FLIM) further resolved intracellular HDL, LDL, and Ox-LDL. Owing to its ultrasmall molecular size, 1j readily penetrated pathological lesions and accumulated at disease-associated sites. By modular installation of a bioorthogonal reactive handle for pretargeting, we achieved combined near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence and microPET/CT multimodal in vivo imaging in hyperlipidemic mice, enabling high-contrast whole-body detection of endogenous lipoproteins with favorable target-to-background ratios. This work establishes a versatile molecular sensing and imaging platform for the spatiotemporal tracking of lipoproteins in biological matrices. The analytical tools presented here meet measurement needs for metabolic liver and cardiovascular

papers.title: Interfacial Electronic Reconstruction Activates TiO2 in MnO2/TiO2 Heterostructures for Accelerated Sulfur Redox Chemistry.
papers.abstract: Lithium-sulfur batteries are promising for next-generation energy storage but are limited by sluggish sulfur redox kinetics originating from insufficient regulation of interfacial electronic structures. Here, we report a MnO2/TiO2 heterostructure with integrated interfacial bonding, in which residual carbon is inherently incorporated into the interfacial region. The characterizations reveal pronounced reconstruction of the local coordination and electronic environment upon heterostructure formation, including Ti─O─Mn bonding, reduced Ti states, and substantial changes in the surface potential and valence-band structure. DFT calculations suggest that the reconstructed interface involves the coexistence of net intercomponent charge redistribution and localized bond polarization, with residual carbon contributing to interfacial electronic coupling. Consistent with this reconstructed electronic environment, Ti-derived sites exhibit enhanced electronic response toward polysulfides, while MnO2 and residual carbon contribute to the coupled interfacial structure. Consequently, MnO2/TiO2 catalyst enables stable cycling under a high sulfur loading of 9.2 mg cm-2 and, when integrated as a functional interlayer, allows the sulfur cathode to deliver a high specific capacity of 1569 mAh g-1 together with durability over 1000 cycles, with a capacity decay rate of 0.054% per cycle. This work highlights chemically integrated oxide heterointerfaces as an effective platform for regulating local electronic structures and accelerating sulfur redox chemistry.

papers.title: End-group electronic stabilization enables energy-dense neutral polynitrogen chains beyond N6.
papers.abstract: Neutral polynitrogen chains are attractive high-energy-density materials because conversion of catenated nitrogen frameworks to N2 can release large amounts of energy. However, extending neutral nitrogen chains beyond the recently isolated open-chain C2h-N6 allotrope remains challenging because of rapid kinetic collapse. Here we introduce end-group electronic stabilization (EGES) as a molecular design principle for supporting extended neutral polynitrogen backbones. Using benchmarked domain-based local pair natural orbital coupled-cluster theory with singles, doubles, and perturbative triples combined with second-order Møller-Plesset perturbation theory [DLPNO-CCSD(T)//MP2], we investigate fluorine-terminated F(N6)nF chains (n = 1-6) as a proof of concept. Terminal fluorination stabilizes the prototype N6 framework by 37.2 kcal mol-1 while preserving its alternating N-N bonding motif. Upon chain extension from FN6F to FN36F, the electronic decomposition energy increases in magnitude to -1131.8 kcal mol-1, corresponding to an electronic mass energy density of 8.73 MJ kg-1. For the N-N cleavage pathways examined, the electronic activation barriers remain within a relatively narrow range of 16.2-19.8 kcal mol-1, showing that increased energy storage does not necessarily cause proportional loss of kinetic protection. NBO, Wiberg bond-order, frontier-orbital, and MESP analyses reveal terminal polarization, partial N-N bond equalization, and cooperative electrostatic organization along the backbone. The progressively more negative MESP minima at nitrogen lone-pair regions, despite nearly unchanged lone-pair occupancies, identify the stabilizing response as collective rather than local. Exergonic XN2X + N6 → XN6X + N2 exchange reactions for several terminal groups indicate that end-group stabilization is a broader strategy, while DFT calculations up to FN60F support structural scalability. These results support end-group control as a route to kinetically metast

papers.title: DNA condensation by 4-arm PEG-histidine/lysine peptide polyplexes: Tuning transfection and biocompatibility.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Gene delivery systems often rely on long polymerized chains lacking structural modularity. This study investigates a modular architecture utilizing a central 4-arm polyethylene glycol (PEG) core as a framework for lysine- and histidine-rich peptides coupled via stable thioether bonds, creating a multifunctional platform with available arms for future targeting ligand attachment. METHODS: Two non-viral vector series were synthesized: one based on a short sequence, Cys-(His)₆-(Lys)₃-(His)₆, and one based on a longer sequence, Cys-(His)₆-(Lys)₃-(His)₆-(Lys)₃-(His)₆, each including the free peptide and conjugates with 2 kDa or 20 kDa 4-arm PEG. Synthesis was confirmed by NMR and MALDI-TOF. Biophysical characterization included AFM, pH-dependent zeta potential, and GelRed displacement assays. Stability was assessed via hydrodynamic diameter monitoring, and biological performance through luciferase transfection, metabolic viability, and oxidative stress assays. RESULTS: The longer peptide exhibited higher DNA-binding affinity and displacement capacity than the shorter variant. The unmodified longer peptide achieved the highest transfection efficiency. The 2 kDa PEG stabilized the shorter peptide polyplexes but sterically hindered the already optimized longer peptide, moderating its efficiency. The 20 kDa PEG produced over-stabilized, network-like structures that inhibited cellular interaction for both peptides. All formulations exhibited a favorable in vitro cytocompatibility profile, with no detectable acute oxidative stress and cell viability generally remaining above the commonly accepted cytotoxicity threshold. CONCLUSION: The 4-arm PEG-peptide architecture represents a modular and tunable platform for the development of non-viral gene delivery systems. papers.title: Ultrasonic-assisted extraction of flaxseed oil with bio-based 2-methyltetrahydrofuran: When thermodynamics meets kinetics.
papers.abstract: Conventional flaxseed oil extraction relies on Soxhlet extraction with petroleum-derived solvent n-hexane, a process burdened by long residence times, high solvent demand, and occupational and environmental hazards. Here, we report an ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) using the green bio-based solvent 2-methyltetrahydrofuran (2-MeTHF). Under optimized conditions (solid-to-liquid ratio of 1:15 g/mL, 5 min, 315 W, no external heating), the UAE/2-MeTHF process gave an oil yield of 0.386 g/g dry mass, i.e. 94 % of the Soxhlet reference (0.411 g g-1), while consuming 0.31-0.33 kWh/ 30 g batch, 23-24 % of the Soxhlet energy demand (1.37-1.71 kWh/ 30 g batch). The protein co-recovered from the defatted meal retained its secondary-structure composition, as shown by ATR-FTIR. Solute-solvent interaction energies from molecular dynamics simulations and thermodynamic calculations showed that 2-MeTHF's solubility advantage arises from hydrogen bonding and van der Waals interactions; its slightly slower self-diffusion relative to n-hexane is compensated by cavitation-enhanced mass transfer. Green Star (96.3 %) and AGREEprep (0.66) assessments ranked the process decisively above UAE/n-hexane (48.1 %; 0.28) and Soxhlet/n-hexane (44 %; 0.22). Five-cycle solvent recycling gave a recovery of 84.5-85.2 %​ (cf. 80.9-81.2 % for n-hexane), with no downward trend in recovery or yield. Overall, ultrasound coupled with a bio-based solvent therefore offers a green, efficient, and technically transferable route for future seed-oil industry.

papers.title: The transition to fatherhood beyond early infancy: Hormonal, behavioral and psychological changes.
papers.abstract: Previous cross-sectional studies have documented hormonal differences between human fathers and nonfathers. However, the timing and persistence of these changes remain unclear. We previously reported that first-time expecting fathers exhibited lower plasma testosterone (T) and arginine vasopressin (AVP), as well as dynamic changes in oxytocin (OT) across portions of the prenatal and early postpartum period compared with partnered nonfather controls. By four months postpartum, however, these group differences were no longer significant. Here, we extend these findings longitudinally into late infancy and early childhood. After controlling for relevant confounds, plasma T, OT, AVP and cortisol levels did not differ significantly between fathers and nonfathers at either one or two years postpartum. Nevertheless, individual differences in paternal hormone levels continued to predict paternal behavior and relationship functioning. At one year postpartum, lower T was associated with greater paternal positive engagement and less frustration with the child, whereas higher cortisol was associated with lower paternal positive engagement. At two years postpartum, higher OT was associated with stronger father-infant attachment. Both fathers and their partners reported declining relationship quality across this period, and mediation analyses suggested that higher T levels mediated the association between reduced time spent with partners and poorer relationship quality. These findings suggest that hormonal changes accompanying the transition to fatherhood may be transient at the group level, while individual variation in paternal hormones continue to relate meaningfully to caregiving, attachment, and relationship functioning into early childhood.

papers.title: Associations Between Sexual Goals, Relationship Satisfaction, and Conflict Among Couples Affected by Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder.
papers.abstract: Engaging in sex to pursue approach goals (e.g., intimacy), is linked with greater relationship satisfaction, whereas avoidance goals (e.g., preventing partner disappointment) relate to lower satisfaction and higher conflict. Compared to those without sexual difficulties, individuals with Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder (SIAD) report fewer approach and more avoidance goals, with potential implications for their relationship quality. To examine bidirectional associations between partner-focused sexual goals and relationship satisfaction and conflict, individuals with SIAD and their partners (N = 263 couples) completed validated measures at baseline and 6 months later. Guided by the actor-partner interdependence model, structural equation models revealed that higher approach goals among individuals with SIAD were associated with greater concurrent relationship satisfaction. In contrast, partners' higher avoidance goals were associated with lower concurrent satisfaction and higher conflict for both couple members. Prospective associations indicated that sexual goals did not predict 6-month outcomes, or vice versa, except that those individuals with SIAD who reported higher baseline relationship satisfaction reported lower avoidance goals 6 months later. Findings highlight that sexual goals mostly relate to proximal experiences of relationship quality in couples facing SIAD, suggesting that promoting approach and reducing avoidance goals may be linked to more favorable outcomes in their sexual relationships.

papers.title: Understanding barriers to meaningful and sustainable community-university collaborations in teaching about social determinants of health: a participatory study allying with community knowledge.
papers.journal: Advances in health sciences education : theory and practice
papers.abstract: Teaching about the social determinants of health (SDOHs) is crucial to training socially engaged healthcare professionals. However, operationalization of SDOHs teaching in health sciences education faces several barriers, which ultimately affect students' capacity to critically think about contemporary social issues. Meanwhile, innovative popular education practices are being developed in community settings to address SDOHs. Despite their transformative potential, these practices are rarely used in universities. Seeing this as a missed opportunity, this article presents the results of a participatory research that identifies the main factors influencing university-community collaborations in teaching SDOHs in the Université Laval's context (Québec, Canada).The participatory project involved a steering committee made up of experts by experience, community organizations representatives, and researchers. The qualitative design used 14 semi-structured interviews with community organizations engaged in awareness-raising and teaching activities on topics related to the SDOHs, targeting various audiences, and 2 focus groups with Université Laval's teaching staff (n=9) with experience of working with community organizations in teaching content related to the SDOHs, providing multiple perspectives on the collaborations. Thematic analysis was co-conducted with members of the steering committee. Key factors affecting university-community collaborations in teaching SDOHs were: (1) the dominant discourse about health and social priorities; (2) two distinct world views; (3) recurring power imbalances; (4) university's commitment and support and (5) characteristics of community organizations. This study is rooted in a critical conception of SDOHs and a deep conviction of the value of community knowledge in SDOHs teaching. papers.title: Dual-phase deep learning recommendation system for radiographic crown lengthening assessment and post selection for the restoration of endodontically treated teeth.
papers.abstract: STATEMENT OF PROBLEM: Restoring endodontically treated teeth requires careful evaluation of the supracrestal tissue attachment, ferrule integrity, and post-space dimensions to ensure long-term success. Manual radiographic analysis for crown lengthening indication and post selection is often time-consuming, subjective, and inconsistent, particularly in resource-limited settings where specialist access may be constrained. PURPOSE: The purpose of this study was to design and validate an artificial intelligence (AI)-driven system that automated 2 essential restorative planning tasks, evaluating the clinical need for crown lengthening and recommending appropriate post dimensions in endodontically treated teeth, using dental radiographs as the input. MATERIAL AND METHODS: Two deep learning pipelines were developed and trained on annotated panoramic and periapical datasets with annotations created under the supervision of dentistry professionals. The crown measurement pipeline employed a U-shaped network (U-Net) model for initial tooth segmentation (assigning unique instance masks to each tooth), then cropping individual teeth and feeding them into a Mask Region-based Convolutional Neural Network (Mask R-CNN) for precise detection and crown length calculation, facilitating the assessment of parameters such as supracrestal tissue attachment and ferrule height, for identification of potential violations or restoration limitations. The post measurement pipeline utilized Mask R-CNN directly on the original images to detect endodontic posts and measure their length and width, enabling comparison against established prosthodontic criteria. Both models were trained in a graphics processing unit (GPU)-enabled environment (Kaggle; Google LLC) and evaluated using standard metrics including Intersection over Union (IoU), Dice coefficient, and measurement accuracy, with validation involving visual overlays and quantitative comparisons to expert annotations. papers.title: Two-dimensional adhesion noise spectroscopy: a CMOS-based, non-invasive modality for real-time cell and tissue monitoring.
papers.abstract: Non-invasive monitoring of cellular adhesion and behavior is essential for lab-on-chip systems, yet current electrical and optical approaches require external stimuli or labels. Here we introduce two-dimensional adhesion noise spectroscopy, a fully passive and label-free electrical imaging modality that repurposes the intrinsic thermal voltage noise of the cell-electrode interface as a real-time indicator of cell attachment. Using four distinct CMOS-based microelectrode array platforms with varying electrode geometries, materials, and amplifier architectures, we show that adherent cells induce a robust increase in voltage noise spectral density, enabling reliable discrimination between cell-covered and electrolyte-covered electrodes. This method generalizes across electrogenic and non-electrogenic cell types, supports continuous tracking of cancer cell proliferation, and identifies active recording sites in ex vivo neural tissue without optical guidance. By requiring only seconds of extracellular recordings and no perturbation of the biological sample, adhesion noise spectroscopy provides a scalable, universally compatible sensing principle for new lab-on-chip interfaces, offering a powerful route toward automated, high-resolution monitoring of cell adhesion, growth, and bio-interface dynamics.

papers.title: Parent and Child Outcomes in a Paediatric Partial Hospital Programme for Restrictive Eating Disorders.
papers.journal: European eating disorders review : the journal of the Eating Disorders Association
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: Anorexia nervosa (AN) and avoidant/restrictive food intake disorder (ARFID) are restrictive eating disorders (EDs) that can onset in childhood, require intensive ED treatment (e.g., a partial hospitalisation programme [PHP]), and overlap or differ in clinical presentation, maintaining mechanisms, and treatment response. Yet, paediatric ED outcomes remain largely unexamined. This study compared outcomes of a paediatric ED PHP across AN and ARFID. METHOD: Parents of children with AN (n = 81) or ARFID (n = 78) completed questionnaires at intake, 1-month, discharge, 6-month follow-up (FU), and 1-year FU; mean child age was 11.38 years (SD = 1.72) at admission. Multilevel models evaluated outcomes measured at intake through FU. The AN and ARFID groups were compared on demographics and clinical characteristics. RESULTS: Child ED symptoms, completion of meals/snacks, child general psychopathology, and parent mental health improved over treatment and follow-up. Those with AN demonstrated greater decreases in internalising and externalising symptoms. ARFID diagnosis corresponded to poorer meal/snack completion, younger age, longer course, and male sex. CONCLUSIONS: In a paediatric ED PHP, youth with AN or ARFID demonstrate similar (e.g., improved parent mental health, weight gain) and differential outcomes (e.g., greater decreases in general psychopathology in AN).

papers.title: Child Sexual Abuse, Sexual Function, and Sexual Distress in Couples Coping with Sexual Interest/Arousal Disorder: A Dyadic Longitudinal Study.
papers.abstract: Sexual interest/arousal disorder (SIAD), characterized by low sexual desire and high sexual distress, is the most common sexual dysfunction among women. Although current theoretical models support interpersonal conceptualizations of sexual desire, distal interpersonal factors that may underlie the sexual well-being of couples coping with SIAD, such as child sexual abuse (CSA), have not been thoroughly documented. Yet, difficulties with sexual desire and arousal are among the most frequently reported sexual dysfunctions among CSA survivors. Using a one-year longitudinal design among couples with SIAD, this study examined the associations between both partners' CSA and their sexual function and distress. Individuals with SIAD (N = 263; Mage = 34.16) and their partners (N = 263; Mage = 35.71) completed validated questionnaires at baseline, 6 months, and 12 months. Dyadic latent growth curve analyses were conducted within a structural equation model. Results showed that greater CSA among individuals with SIAD was associated with their own higher initial levels of sexual distress. Moreover, higher levels of non-SIAD partners' CSA were unexpectedly associated with lower initial levels of sexual function difficulties for individuals with SIAD. However, non-SIAD partners' CSA predicted greater increases in sexual function difficulties over time for individuals with SIAD. No other significant associations were found. Findings highlight the role of CSA in the sexual function and distress of couples coping with SIAD and point towards the value of couple-based interventions that acknowledge both partners' histories and their impact on mutual sexual experiences.

papers.title: Acceptability of a multimodal intervention for provoked vulvodynia: results from the mixed-methods pilot phase of the Vulvodynia Intervention project.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: Provoked vulvodynia (PVD) is a chronic vulvar pain condition associated with substantial negative effects on physical, psychological and relational health. Although clinical guidelines recommend multimodal treatment approaches, systematic evaluations remain limited. The aim of this pilot-phase study is to evaluate the acceptability of a multimodal intervention for PVD and assess the feasibility of study procedures and outcome measures to inform a future full-scale clinical trial. DESIGN: Pilot study with mixed-methods design, integrating qualitative interviews with quantitative pretreatment and post-treatment assessments. This work represents the pilot phase of the ongoing Vulvodynia Intervention project. SETTING: Two specialised healthcare units in Sweden providing care for vulvodynia. Clinical teams consisted of gynaecologists responsible for diagnosis, while psychologists and physiotherapists delivered the treatment, with regular supervision to ensure consistency across sites. PARTICIPANTS: Six women aged 21–28 years with PVD were enrolled. One discontinued the intervention for reasons unrelated to treatment, one was paused and four completed the intervention. Five were included in the analyses. INTERVENTION: A multimodal intervention grounded in cognitive behavioural therapy and behavioural medicine, integrating biomedical, psychological and social components. The programme comprised 10 individual sessions over 4 months and a booster session after 3 months. Treatment was primarily delivered digitally, with two on-site physiotherapy sessions and optional partner involvement. MEASURES: Intervention acceptability was assessed through qualitative interviews. Additional measures were used to evaluate the feasibility of study procedures and self-report measures assessing physical, psychological and relational factors. RESULTS: Participants described the intervention as acceptable, helpful and coherent, though demanding. They reported i

papers.title: Sexual functioning in women with anorexia nervosa: a cross-sectional study among Slovak and Czech respondents.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Research on sexual functioning in women with anorexia nervosa (AN) remains limited in Central Europe. This study is among the first conducted in Slovakia and adds to limited existing Czech research. It aimed to compare sexual functioning between sexually active women with AN and healthy controls in Slovakia and the Czech Republic. METHODS: In this cross-sectional study, women with current or previous AN (N = 48) and controls (N = 74) completed anonymous online or paper-based questionnaires, including the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI) and Eating Disorder Examination Questionnaire-Short Form (EDE-QS). Because the FSFI is applicable only to sexually active women, FSFI analyses were restricted to sexually active participants (N = 27 clinic, N = 69 controls). RESULTS: Sexually active women with AN reported significantly lower overall sexual functioning than controls (FSFI median: 20 vs. 28.9, p < 0.001), ​with lower scores across the assessed FSFI domains. In the AN group, greater eating disorder (ED) symptom severity was associated with poorer sexual functioning, whereas body mass index and partnership status were not significantly associated. CONCLUSIONS: Sexually active women with AN reported lower FSFI than healthy controls. Higher ED symptom scores were associated with lower FSFI scores. These findings are consistent with existing evidence supporting attention to sexual health in clinical assessment and care, although the cross-sectional design precludes conclusions about directionality or causality.

papers.title: Two Persons, One Womb: Testing the Social Construction of Reproduction in Conjoined Twins.
papers.abstract: Standard models of reproductive autonomy presuppose a singular and bounded subject. This paper challenges that assumption by analysing the limit case of dicephalus parapagus conjoined twins where two distinct persons share a single reproductive system. I argue that this physiological configuration creates an ontological indeterminacy that biological essentialism cannot resolve. Drawing on a previous constructivist framework of reproduction, I demonstrate that when gestation is a shared biological event but personhood is distinct, the designation of "mother" cannot be discovered in the tissue but must be acknowledged through intention. The analysis proceeds to examine the severe ethical conflict arising when one twin wishes to reproduce while the other does not. I contend that prioritizing the reproductive desire of one sister over the refusal of the other constitutes a violation of bodily integrity analogous to involuntary gestational surrogacy. Consequently, I argue that in shared bodies, the non-reproducing person must hold an absolute power of veto. This aligns with established bioethical precedents, such as those discussed by Robertson, where the right to avoid involuntary biological parenthood is often held to supersede a former partner's desire to gestate shared embryos. Finally, this paper posits that the principles derived from this extreme case offer a necessary heuristic for broader bioethical issues. The example of conjoined twins validates the distributed maternity of Reciprocal IVF in lesbian couples while simultaneously reinforcing the protections against coercive surrogacy. By deconstructing the most extreme form of shared biology, this paper offers an exploration of a case of fragmented maternity and its implications.

papers.title: Health Decision-Making Among Women Survivors of Intimate Partner Violence: A Scoping Review.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intimate partner violence (IPV) affects approximately one in four women worldwide, with profound consequences for physical, mental, and reproductive health. Autonomy in health decision-making is central to women's health, yet IPV undermines survivors' capacity to make free and informed choices about their own care. A comprehensive synthesis of the barriers and supporting factors to this autonomy is still lacking. Such understanding is essential for equipping healthcare providers with the evidence needed to recognize abuse, respond effectively, and support affected women. METHODS: This scoping review followed Arksey and O'Malley's five-stage framework and the PRISMA-ScR guidelines. PubMed, CINAHL, PsycINFO, and Scopus were searched in May 2023, with an update in October 2026. Studies were eligible if they examined health decision-making in relation to IPV, including associated sociodemographic and contextual factors, among women survivors, with no restrictions on publication date or study design. RESULTS: The 23 included studies were conducted in South Asia (n = 7), the United States (n = 7), Sub-Saharan Africa (n = 3), Australia (n = 2), the United Kingdom (n = 2), East Asia (n = 1), and the Middle East (n = 1), with an aggregate population of 192,532 participants. Three overlapping domains were identified: reproductive and maternal health decisions (n = 7), healthcare-seeking and disclosure decisions (n = 12), and safety and support-seeking decisions (n = 11). Key barriers included fear of retaliation, stigma, financial dependence, low educational attainment, patriarchal control, reproductive coercion, limited knowledge of resources, and unresponsive healthcare encounters, whereas facilitators included empathic and confidential provider engagement, knowledge of rights, personal resilience, and support from family, friends, and formal services. CONCLUSIONS: Health decision-making among IPV survivors was shaped by intersecting individual, structural, and

papers.title: American Femicide as a Function of Gun Access and Ownership: A Comparison of 2 States.
papers.journal: The American journal of forensic medicine and pathology
papers.abstract: Femicide is the intentional killing of a woman where her gender played a role in the reason she was killed. Femicide is a specific subset of violence perpetrated against women. This study aimed to compare the rates of femicide between 2 states, Connecticut (CT) and New Hampshire (NH). Both are relatively small states in New England; however, their approaches to gun control differ significantly. The Gabby Giffords Gun Law scorecard was used as a surrogate to examine state-level gun access, with NH having much more lax laws than CT. The investigative narrative was examined for female homicides in each state from 2012 to 2024 to classify the homicide as a femicide, nonfemicide, or unknown (n=446). It was found that the rate of femicide caused by firearms was higher in NH (P=0.015), but the overall rate of femicide between the 2 states did not differ. When comparing CT femicides to nonfemicides, it was found that asphyxia and sharp force injuries were more common in femicides. There may be a substitution of violence in CT towards nonfirearm modalities of cause of death since firearms are not as readily available. State-level legislation for gun control and access may not alter rates of violence against women.

papers.title: Maternal exposure to intimate partner violence and child stunting from birth through 5 years: evidence from a South African longitudinal birth cohort study.
Trauma in Pregnancy.
papers.journal: Emergency medicine clinics of North America
papers.abstract: Trauma is the leading cause of death in reproductive-aged individuals, complicating 6% to 8% of pregnancies and accounting for approximately 20% of maternal deaths. This article reviews a maternal-first resuscitation approach, emphasizing that fetal survival hinges on maternal stabilization. It details pregnancy-specific alterations affecting the primary survey including difficult airway, respiratory compensation, aortocaval compression, and delayed recognition of hemorrhagic shock. It also provides guidance on blood product resuscitation, RhD considerations, TXA, and resuscitative hysterotomy. Diagnostic evaluation covers imaging recommendations and laboratory nuances. Finally, it addresses mechanism-specific injuries, intimate partner violence, fetal monitoring, patient counseling, and criteria for discharge.

papers.title: Modeling Intimate Partner Violence Exposure Risk Among University Students in Barbados: A Machine Learning Approach.
papers.abstract: This study examines intimate partner violence (IPV) exposure among Barbadian university students utilizing data from the American College Health Association National College Health Assessment. Using clustered probability proportionate to size without random replacement, a sample size of 599 was required, and 649 students completed the survey. Machine learning, specifically eXtreme Gradient Boosting, identified predictors of IPV. Parental education level emerged as the most influential predictor, followed by relationship status and sexual orientation. Students whose parents had associate degrees or technical training were at higher risk of experiencing IPV compared with those whose parents had either lower or higher levels of education. Additionally, married or partnered students and members of sexual minority groups (e.g., identifying as gay, queer, or "other") reported higher rates of violence exposure. These findings provide insights into IPV patterns among Barbadian university students and the complex interplay of sociodemographic factors in predicting violence exposure.

papers.title: Informal help-seeking among Peruvian women exposed to intimate partner violence: A cross-sectional analysis of violence characteristics in the 2023 Demographic and Health Survey.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intimate partner violence (IPV) is a major public health problem in Peru, yet many women who experience it do not seek help. We examined how the characteristics of IPV and individual and sociocultural factors are associated with help-seeking among Peruvian women exposed to physical and/or sexual IPV. METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of the 2023 Peruvian Demographic and Health Survey (ENDES). The analytic sample comprised 5,584 women aged 15-49 years who reported lifetime physical and/or sexual violence by a current or former partner and were asked whether they had ever sought help. Guided by the help-seeking model, we fitted three nested, survey-weighted logistic regression models (individual, interpersonal, and sociocultural factors), accounting for the complex sampling design. Discrimination was assessed with the area under the ROC curve (AUC). We also examined the number of IPV types experienced (emotional, physical, sexual). RESULTS: Overall, 45.0% (95% CI 42.4-47.7) of women had sought help; the most frequent reasons for not doing so were thinking it was not necessary (41.2%) and shame (16.2%). In the fully adjusted model, help-seeking was more likely among women who experienced severe physical IPV (OR 1.51; 95% CI 1.15-1.98), emotional IPV (OR 1.33; 1.05-1.67), and health problems due to violence (OR 2.22; 1.75-2.81), and was slightly less likely with increasing age (OR 0.99 per year; 0.97-1.00). Sexual IPV, region, area of residence, household wealth, and sex of the household head were not associated with help-seeking. Compared with women who experienced one type of IPV, those who experienced two (OR 1.40; 1.11-1.77) or three types (OR 1.70; 1.24-2.35) were more likely to seek help. The interpersonal model discriminated moderately (AUC 0.65); adding sociocultural factors did not improve it. CONCLUSIONS: Among Peruvian women exposed to physical and/or sexual IPV, help-seeking is concentrated among those whose violence is more severe

papers.title: Addressing sensitivity bias in survey questions on sexual behaviour, sexual health, drug consumption, and intimate partner violence in an urban adult population of Tanzania.
papers.abstract: Health behaviour that increases risk is stigmatized in many societies, leading to potential misreporting in surveys designed to capture such behaviour. This sensitivity bias can distort the conclusions drawn from such surveys, thereby influencing policy decisions. Identifying and addressing sensitivity bias in survey questions is crucial to ensure more accurate prevalence estimates and to inform effective policymaking. In this study, we measured sensitivity bias in ten sensitive questions on sexual behaviour, sexual health, drug consumption, and intimate partner violence in a sample of 2270 adults in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania. The data was collected between 19 June 2017 and 24 July 2018. The sensitivity bias was estimated by comparing responses to list experiments with responses to corresponding direct questions. We measured the presence of sensitivity bias in the total sample and analysed heterogeneities by demographic characteristics. We found sensitivity bias in questions on drug use, intimate partner violence, having had sex with multiple partners, and sexual health. Sensitivity bias for the question on transactional sex was negative, implying an overreporting in the direct question. We did not find sensitivity bias for outcomes related to alcohol consumption. Heterogeneities by demographic characteristics were most pronounced between men and women. We conclude that what is considered sensitive among survey respondents is highly context specific. List experiments may help in detecting and minimizing sensitivity bias in sensitive survey questions, but their accuracy is sensitive to several design features and implementation details.

papers.title: Prevalence of intimate partner violence against women in East Africa: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Intimate partner violence (IPV) remains a pervasive public health and human rights issue worldwide, with sub-Saharan Africa (SSA) bearing a disproportionately high burden. However, synthesized evidence specifically from the East African region is limited. METHODS: A systematic review and meta-analysis were conducted following PRISMA guidelines. Forty-one cross-sectional studies reporting IPV among women in East Africa were identified from seven electronic databases (PubMed, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science, African Journals Online [AJOL], CINAHL, and Google Scholar). Databases were searched from August 1 to September 30, 2025.Study quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) critical appraisal checklist for prevalence studies. A random-effects inverse-variance model was used to estimate pooled prevalence with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic. Subgroup analyses were performed by country, population, study setting, recall period, IPV type, publication year, sample size, and data collection tool. Publication bias was assessed via funnel plots, Egger's test, and the trim-and-fill method. Sensitivity analysis was conducted using leave-one-out procedures. RESULTS: The meta-analysis included 41 studies. The overall pooled prevalence of IPV was 42.8% (95% CI: 38.3-47.9%), indicating high heterogeneity (I2 = 99.6%). Subgroup analyses revealed significant variation: the highest prevalence was among contraceptive users (72.6%, based on a single study) and ever-married/partnered women (55.1%), while the lowest was among refugees (31.0%) and in large-scale studies (32.9%). Country-level estimates were highest in Uganda (52.0%), followed by Tanzania (49.9%) and Ethiopia (44.5%), and lowest in Rwanda (20.9%). Studies using WHO standard tools reported higher prevalence (49.1%) than those using DHS modules (36.3%) No significant publication bias was detected (Egger's test *p* = 0.

papers.title: Attitudes toward intimate partner violence and survey-derived mental health symptom indicators among young women in Kazakhstan: findings from the Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey in Kazakhstan.
papers.abstract: PURPOSE: Previous studies demonstrated the influence of intimate partner violence (IPV) on mental health, however, there is a lack of studies exploring the influence of social norms and perceptions of IPV on the emotional well-being of women. This study aimed to examine the association between attitudes toward intimate partner violence and survey-derived mental health symptom indicators among young women in Kazakhstan. METHODS: This study was based on secondary data from the Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey 2024. The sample included 3324 women aged 15-24 years across 17 regions and three large cities in Kazakhstan. Descriptive, bivariate and multivariate logistic regression methods were used for analyses, accounting for survey design effects (Stata 18.0). RESULTS: The prevalence of depressive symptom indicators was 3.76% (95% CI: 3.12-4.53), while the rate of anxiety symptom indicators was 6.73% (95% CI: 5.70-7.92). The prevalence of either depression or anxiety symptom indicators was 8.32% (95% CI: 7.20-9.59). Women who justified IPV had significantly higher odds of depression symptom indicators (aOR = 3.31, 95% CI:1.33-8.25), anxiety symptom indicators (aOR = 5.33, 95% CI: 2.63-10.84), and symptom indicators of depression and/or anxiety (aOR = 4.09, 95% CI: 2.08-8.05) compared to those who did not endorse IPV, after adjusting for covariates. Factors such as age, wealth index, specific regions, and relationship status demonstrated significant association with women's mental health symptom indicators. CONCLUSION: This study found that justification of IPV was significantly associated with mental health symptom indicators. The findings may inform broader policy discussions concerning gender norms and violence prevention by highlighting the association between attitudes toward violence against women and women's mental health. Further research incorporating measures of IPV exposure is needed to clarify this relations

papers.title: Cumulative social determinants of health and long-term health outcomes among survivors of childhood sexual abuse: A retrospective chart review.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Childhood sexual abuse (CSA) is associated with long-term adverse physical, mental, and reproductive health outcomes. However, less is known about how cumulative social determinants of health (SDOH) further stratify risk within this population. OBJECTIVE: To evaluate associations between cumulative SDOH exposure and long-term health outcomes among adult survivors of CSA. PARTICIPANTS AND SETTING: A retrospective chart review of 70 adult CSA survivors receiving care at a large urban academic medical center in the Midwestern United States between 2015 and 2024. METHODS: Cumulative indices of SDOH exposure (housing instability, food insecurity, intimate partner violence, and transportation barriers) and chronic disease burden were constructed. Multivariable linear and logistic regression models assessed associations with physical, mental, and reproductive health outcomes and examined potential modification by psychosocial factors. RESULTS: Higher cumulative SDOH exposure was associated with increased chronic physical disease burden and greater odds of reproductive complications among female patients, demonstrating a dose-response relationship. The association with chronic physical disease burden remained significant after adjustment for psychosocial factors, with similar effect estimates observed in sensitivity analyses accounting for demographic and socioeconomic variables. No significant associations were observed for chronic mental health conditions. CONCLUSIONS: Social and structural disadvantage further stratifies long-term health risk among CSA survivors. Findings support integration of SDOH screening within trauma-informed care models to improve long-term outcomes in this population.

papers.title: Parent-Adolescent and Peer Relationship Quality, Academic Pressure, and Depressive Symptoms in Chinese Late Adolescents: Latent Growth Curve Model Combined With Network Analysis.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: The close relevance between adolescents' academic pressure, depressive symptoms, and interpersonal relationships with parents and peers has been well-documented in extant literature. However, few studies have examined the developmental trajectories of these variables and how they dynamically relate to one another over time. METHODS: Using data from three waves spaced 8 months apart and integrating Latent Growth Curve Modeling (LGCM) with network analysis, this study explored both the average levels and the rates of change over time in these variables. The participants were Chinese high school students (n = 643, Mage = 16.87, SD = 0.55; 44.3% male). RESULTS: Results revealed that both depressive symptoms and peer relationship quality increased over time. Depressive symptoms and academic pressure were positively associated at both the average level and in their developmental trajectories, indicating a parallel pattern of co-development. Moreover, average levels of parent-adolescent and peer relationship quality were negatively correlated with the average levels but not the slopes of both depressive symptoms and academic pressure over time. CONCLUSIONS: These results highlight the importance of monitoring academic and emotional indicators simultaneously, rather than in isolation, to better understand and support adolescents' adaptive functioning. Interpersonal relationship quality emerges as a potential candidate for identifying adolescents who may be at risk for elevated academic pressure and depressive symptoms.
